Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.label: mechanical power
Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.guideText:
Machines marked as power consumers do not run on electricity. They need rotary power from a mechanical network.
Building a network - Place the small steam engine so it touches the machine, including diagonally. Every touching power source, consumer and line shaft joins the same network. - Select any connected building and open the mechanical network tab to see total output, demand and overload.
Fuel - The small steam engine burns wood while it is switched on. A full load of 25 wood lasts about half a day, and colonists refuel it automatically below 75%. - Keep a wood stockpile nearby and let haulers and builders reach it. An empty engine stops every machine on its network, including coolers and freezers.
Load - The small steam engine supplies 1,500 W normally and up to 1,800 W at most. Each machine lists its rated mechanical input; idle worktables draw only part of it. - When demand exceeds maximum output, shaft speed falls. Machines below their minimum speed stop, overloaded machines can cause accidents, and a badly overloaded steam engine can be damaged or explode. - Switch off machines you are not using, or add another power source to the network.
Production buildings that need power cannot take bills while their network is down, and work in progress pauses until power returns.

Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.label: line shafts
Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.guideText:
Line shafts carry rotary power between buildings that do not touch.
- Lay line shafts like conduits from a power source to each machine. Each segment links to the buildings and shafts touching it. - Everything joined by shafts becomes one network. All power sources on it add their output, and all machines share it. - Separate shaft lines form separate networks. Keep critical equipment, such as coolers and freezers, on a network whose demand stays below its power sources' normal output. - Check the mechanical network tab after expanding. If several worktables run at once, demand can pass the maximum output and slow every machine on the line.

Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.label: the telegraph
Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.guideText:
The telegraph connects the colony to LOW Helod companies and organizations.
Opening a line 1. Build the telegraph. It needs an interaction spot and a constructor with Construction 5. 2. Wait for a LOW Helod caravan to visit the colony and request line installation from it. Installation costs 250 STL. 3. The line opens 2–3 days later, and a letter announces it.
Using the line - A colonist operates the telegraph to contact companies. The relay is open from 08:00 to 18:00 local time; faction and company rows can be expanded only during those hours. - Available services include financial, industrial, arms and hunting, and petroleum caravans, Pioneer Overseas Service Company forward-base contracts, and Harrington Protective Services guards. - Caravan requests require financial reputation. - Each transmission uses primary cells. Keep primary cells stocked so the telegraph can be refueled.
The radio, unlocked later, offers the same services with electricity instead of a wired line and primary cells.

Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.label: oil development
Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.guideText:
Crude oil comes from wells that the colony drills itself.
Drilling 1. Build a cable-tool rig on heavy ground and connect it to a mechanical network. 2. The rig drills while it has power. It regularly stops for maintenance; a colonist must service it before drilling continues. 3. After about seven days of drilling, sometimes earlier, the ground becomes an oil field. Cable-tool wells have 75–80% quality.
Pumping - Deconstruct the rig and build a basic pump jack on the developed oil field. The pump jack also needs mechanical power. - Field quality and declining well pressure determine extraction speed. The pump jack's inspect panel shows both.
Refining - The batch still distills heavy crude oil into one selected product per bill: diesel, kerosene, chemfuel or naphtha. - To seal an exhausted well, remove the rig and pump first, then use Remove floor on the oil field.

Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.label: electric generation
Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.guideText:
Motors and generators link the mechanical network with the electrical grid.
Early industrial generator - Connect the generator to a mechanical network and to electrical conduits. It turns shaft power into electricity. - Set its target electrical output. The target decides how much shaft power it draws, so a high target can overload the mechanical network. - Efficiency rises from 60% at low load to 80% at its 10 kW rated input.
Large industrial motor - The motor works in the other direction: it draws electricity and supplies rotary power to a mechanical network. - If an electric motor is overloaded, it can short-circuit or violently discharge a battery on its grid.

Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.label: the radio
Helodrace.Research.ResearchGuideDef.guideText:
The radio replaces the telegraph's wired line.
- Build the radio and connect it to electricity. It consumes 80 W while switched on. - It needs no line installation and no primary cells, and company frequencies are available around the clock. - It offers every telegraph service: caravan requests, loans, forward-base contracts and security. - Colonists also use it for recreation, chatting on LOW and HIGH HAM frequencies or listening to broadcasts from nearby seats.
